note: Historical teaching data; PAID renamed claim_amount. Week 2 needs faults to clean, and AutoClaims has none, so missingness is INJECTED by three distinct mechanisms with set.seed(5109) - age MAR on class (599, 8.8%), gender MCAR (297, 4.4%), claim_amount MNAR on the top decile (133, 2.0%) - plus 1 negative, 1 zero and 3 duplicated rows. Rates were chosen by criterion, not taste: each column's complete-case bias is at least three standard errors, row-level incompleteness reaches 14.7% (993 of 6776, which is what justifies multiple imputation), and no column exceeds 10%, and the header is rewritten to Claim No/State/CLASS/Gender/Age/Claim Amount - none of this is in the source. The claim_no key is assigned BEFORE the copies, which separates three duplicate cases: duplicated(rows)=2 exact copies, duplicated(claim_no)=3 adding one key collision with a conflicting age (95/59), duplicated(profile)=11 - and that third number is NOT the one the copies predict. The copies and the source's own 3 same-profile pairs account for only 4 of it, which is exactly the counter measured among complete rows; the other 7 are manufactured by the missingness injection itself, because blanking a field makes two rows that differed only there identical. Running distinct() over the profile would therefore delete 7 genuinely different records.
